stories.title: 🙏 Prayer of Manasseh
summaryBullets: O Lord Almighty, God of our ancestors, of Abraham and Isaac and Jacob and of their righteous offspring, (1:1).
you who made heaven and earth with all their order, (1:2).
who shackled the sea by your word of command, who confined the deep and sealed it with your terrible and glorious name, (1:3).
at whom all things shudder and tremble before your power, (1:4).
for your glorious splendor cannot be borne, and the wrath of your threat to sinners is unendurable; (1:5).
yet immeasurable and unsearchable is your promised mercy, (1:6).

for you are the Lord Most High, of great compassion, long-suffering, and very merciful, and you relent at human suffering. O Lord, according to your great goodness you have promised repentance and forgiveness to those who have sinned against you, and in the multitude of your mercies you have appointed repentance for sinners, so that they may be saved. (1:7).

Therefore you, O Lord, God of the righteous, have not appointed repentance for the righteous, for Abraham and Isaac and Jacob, who did not sin against you, but you have appointed repentance for me, who am a sinner. (1:8).

For the sins I have committed are more in number than the sand of the sea; my transgressions are multiplied, O Lord, they are multiplied! I am not worthy to look up and see the height of heaven because of the multitude of my iniquities. (1:9).

I am weighted down with many an iron fetter, so that I am rejected because of my sins, and I have no relief, for I have provoked your wrath and have done what is evil in your sight, setting up abominations and multiplying offenses. (1:10).
And now I bend the knee of my heart, imploring you for your kindness. (1:11).
I have sinned, O Lord, I have sinned, and I acknowledge my transgressions. (1:12).

I earnestly implore you, forgive me, O Lord, forgive me! Do not destroy me with my transgressions! Do not be angry with me forever or store up evil for me; do not condemn me to the depths of the earth. For you, O Lord, are the God of those who repent, (1:13).
and in me you will manifest your goodness, for, unworthy as I am, you will save me according to your great mercy, (1:14).
and I will praise you continually all the days of my life. For all the host of heaven sings your praise, and yours is the glory forever. Amen. (1:15).
crossRefs: 2 Chronicles 33:11-13: Manasseh is taken to Babylon in bronze fetters, humbles himself, and prays.
2 Kings 21:1-9: Manasseh sets up altars and abominations in Jerusalem and Judah.
Job 38:8-11: God shuts in the sea with doors and fixes the bound it cannot pass.
Psalm 51:1-4: A confession of transgression and a plea for mercy.
Luke 18:13: A man who will not lift his eyes to heaven asks God for mercy.

translationNotes.term: Weighted down with many an iron fetter
translationNotes.note: Prisoner's irons at the wrists and ankles, not a figure of speech. 2 Chronicles 33:11 records that the commanders of the king of Assyria took Manasseh with hooks, bound him with bronze fetters, and carried him to Babylon. That captivity is the setting of the prayer.

translationNotes.term: More in number than the sand of the sea
translationNotes.original: Hebrew: כְּחוֹל הַיָּם (ke-hol ha-yam) - Greek: ὑπὲρ ἀριθμὸν ψάμμου θαλάσσης (hyper arithmon psammou thalasses)
translationNotes.note: A standing Hebrew idiom for a quantity past counting, used elsewhere for Abraham's descendants and for the size of armies. It is not a claim about an exact total; it means the count cannot be taken.

translationNotes.term: I bend the knee of my heart
translationNotes.original: Greek: κάμπτω γόνυ καρδίας (kampto gony kardias)
translationNotes.note: Kneeling was the physical posture of a petitioner before a king. The phrase moves the gesture inward and describes the submission itself rather than the position of the body, which matters for a man speaking in irons.

The Greek word means a change of mind and a turn of purpose, not merely feeling sorry. When the prayer says God has 'appointed repentance for sinners,' it means He established a way back, not that He assigned an emotion.

stories.keyTakeaway: Manasseh praises the God who made heaven and earth and shackled the sea, then says God appointed repentance for sinners like him. His sins outnumber the sand of the sea; weighted with iron fetters, he bends the knee of his heart, begs forgiveness, and vows lifelong praise.
